Stephanie / Laura / Jake — draft attached. See notes below and the two sample artifacts attached: sample_audit_snapshot.csv (1 hour slice) and export_checksums.txt.

Executive summary (short):
- Event coverage: Redwood's audit ledger captures authentication events (token and API key usage), authorization decisions (role grants, policy updates), admin configuration changes (deploy/rollback, model version pinning), model invocation metadata (model id, input length, latencies), and data access events for stored artifacts (embeddings, dataset retrieval) when applicable. Sensitive content redaction is applied per customer configuration for hosted deployments.
- Retention: Default retention (hosted) = 90 days for high-volume telemetry, 12 months for admin and security audit events. Dedicated customers can configure retention via the Console; Private deployments run per-customer retention policy controlled by on-prem config (examples in attached playbook).
- Export mechanics: Exports are generated by the Audit Export Service. Supported formats: CSV, NDJSON, parquet. Filters: time-range, event-type, resource-id, tenant-id. Snapshots can be point-in-time (consistent snapshot using the ledger sequence id) or incremental (ordered batches). Exports include dataset manifest and optional gzipped archive.
- Integrity & chain-of-custody: Each export includes a manifest file with SHA256 checksums for each exported file and a signed manifest (HMAC-SHA256 with customer or Redwood key, depending on agreement). For managed delivery to customer S3, we provide presigned PUT URLs or server-side push with TLS. For forensic handoffs, we generate a signed delivery receipt and optional notarization (third-party timestamping) upon request.
- SLA & delivery: Standard export turnaround for requests < 48 hours is 3 business days. For emergency forensics (production incident + SOC2 audit), expedited timeline is 24 hours with an agreed support engagement. Export delivery modes: downloadable link from Console (HTTPS), direct push to customer-managed S3, or encrypted transfer via SFTP.

Security notes and configuration caveats:
- Hosted customers: default redaction and automatic key rotation; additional retention/archival must be requested in contract.
- Dedicated: retention policies are configurable via the Console; exports can be scheduled and automated.
- Private: customer controls retention; Redwood provides export tooling and runbooks for on-prem extraction.

Attachments included:
- redwood_audit_export_playbook.pdf (playbook with step-by-step export runs, examples, and manifest spec)
- sample_audit_snapshot.csv (CSV sample: columns = event_time, event_type, user_id, actor_ip, resource_type, resource_id, action, request_id, model_id, seq_id)
- export_checksums.txt (SHA256 checksums for files in the sample archive)

Open items for Acme / questions:
1) Do you prefer delivery to an Acme-managed S3 bucket (we'll produce presigned PUTs) or direct HTTPS download?
2) Do you require manifest signing with your own public key vs Redwood-managed signing? If the former, we'll need your key (PEM) and a contact for key exchange.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want a walkthrough.

—Dylan Brooks
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Events captured: authn, authz, admin config, model invocation metadata, data access events (see playbook p.4 for full event taxonomy).
- Retention windows: hosted default 90 days for telemetry/12 months for admin/security; Dedicated configurable; Private per-customer.
- Export formats & snapshots: CSV/NDJSON/parquet; point-in-time snapshots via ledger seq_id; incremental exports supported.
- Integrity: manifest with SHA256 checksums + signed manifest (we can sign with Redwood HSM key or with your provided key).
- Delivery & SLA: HTTPS download, presigned S3 PUT, or SFTP; standard 3 business days, expedited 24 hours for incidents with support engagement.
